- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model consistently overpredicts in early forecast windows (e.g., first 5–7 days) — apply downward bias for short-term horizon.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model fails to recognize — reduce forecast slope after peak.
- Sentiment history with multiple 0.00 or 0.14 values suggests low confidence; model overreacts — dampen forecast volatility.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is rising, model underestimates upside — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit above 0.5.
